roles.implementer: Qualification unit of the 2026-09-25 SOTA-refresh workflow: installed the candidate into a new prefix and ran every step below for both arms without touching production.
roles.verifier: A separate agent that re-ran the implementer's steps with its own probe code, checked integrity independently and returned the verdict and defects below.
roles.coordinator: The coordinating session that performed the production switch and the post-switch checks (coordinator observations, exported as the aggregate facts in cutover.json).
roles.writing_worker: The session that assembled this directory; it performed only the read-only production read-back in out/readback.out.

Files marked byte_identical_to_run_copy are the exact bytes that ran or were written; for the others run_copy_sha256 is the digest of the unsanitized run copy, which stays in session scratch.

differences: No regression on the probed surface. Every check that passed on the 2.3.2 baseline also passed on 2.4.0, run against the same backup with the same serve flags as production.
/healthz: 2.4.0 returns 200 {"status":"ok"}; 2.3.2 returns 404. The route is new, and it is a cheap version discriminator.
memory_status: 2.4.0 adds a scope object (resolved_by "explicit" for an explicit workspace/project call) and counts.evidence_rows (0). 2.3.2 has no scope field.

Schema: 2.4.0 migrates V64 -> V66 (66 rows) at startup. No pre-migration archive was written: nothing in AI_MEMORY_BACKUP_DIR, the scratch HOME, the real HOME or <data_dir>/backups, and no pre-migration-backup.json. After that, 2.3.2 serve exits 1 with DataSchemaAhead (naming V65 page_compacted_marker) and leaves the store intact at V66 with quick_check=ok.

Unchanged between versions: 23 MCP tools with identical names, protocol 2024-11-05, stateless transport (GET /mcp 405 with allow: POST), allowlist capture semantics (marker true/true, no marker false/false, nothing spooled by --check-capture), FTS parity, and the embedding identity (local all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384-d, 0 missing). The known-page body sha256 is identical (98eb1dfb...a356).
The 2.3.2 hook client posting to a 2.4.0 server was captured: the nonce was found via an explicit session_id. This contradicts the 2026-09-23 claim that stock 2.3.2 hooks abort against a 2.4.0 store.

Both versions report embedding status 'unknown' after a fresh start, until the first embedding call. The reviewer's startup status expectation of 'embedding ok' would fail on either version, so embedding health must be read after a write or query. This caused baseline attempt 1 to fail.

One count difference comes from probe design only. The 2.4.0 arm ran one extra marker session (the 2.3.2-client probe), so it ends at 37 pages and 71,340 observations versus 36 and 71,337 on 2.3.2. Each completed hook session added one page in both versions.
production_untouched_during_qualificatio:
Before and after snapshots were taken read-only, at 18:57:01Z and 19:03:42Z, and compared with prod-compare.

**Unchanged:**
- nativestack-memory.service kept MainPID 465, ExecMainStartTimestamp 'Thu 2026-09-24 00:23:13 EDT', the same InvocationID hash and NRestarts 0. It was never stopped or restarted.
- ~/.local/share/codex-ecosystem/bin/ai-memory resolved to tools/ai-memory-2.3.2/ai-memory before and after.
- The 2.3.2 binary sha256 stayed 93eeb299...cfed0.
- ~/.codex/hooks.json sha256 stayed e705a4b1....
- Hook commands were 8 Claude plus 7 Codex on 2.3.2, and 0 on 2.4.0, both times.
- Live DB fingerprint, opened mode=ro: 'V64 -> V64 (64 rows) quick_check=ok | pages before=35 missing_or_changed=0 after=35 | observations before=71265 missing=0 after=71812 | PASS'. The growth comes from live sessions' hooks.
- The live /healthz (404) and GET /mcp (405, allow: POST) responses were identical.
- There was no pre-migration-backup.json and no ~/ai-memory-backup-* archive, before or after.

**No probe leakage:**
- 0 hits for all 10 probe tokens in live observations, pages and wiki files.
- 0 of the 7 probe session ids in live sessions.
- nsr-probe and ai-memory-acceptance rows: 0 before and 0 after.
- The tokens were never printed, so the live hooks could not capture them from this session's tool output.
- After the run, the only ai-memory listener is 127.0.0.1:49474, and no scratch ai-memory process remains.

**How live paths were avoided:**
- No command ran with --data-dir on the live store. The backup client used a private scratch data dir and reached the live 2.3.2 server by URL. Its online backup is a server-side SQLite snapshot, with no write to the store.
- Every scratch ai-memory process got an environment built from scratch: HOME set to an empty private scratch home, which was still empty at the end, and AI_MEMORY_SERVER_URL set to the scratch port. This matters because this host exports the live URL into agent shells.
- Nothing touched the GPU servers, systemd, ~/.codex, MCP configs, git checkouts or ~/.local/share/codex-ecosystem/downloads.

**The one failed check:** ~/.claude/settings.json changed (sha256 ddfcbf6d... -> cc635f9f..., mtime 19:01:59.96Z). This run did not cause it:
- The change fell between baseline attempt 1 (results written 19:00:24Z) and attempt 2 (started 19:02:35Z), when no scratch ai-memory process existed.
- install-hooks was never run.
- No scratch process could see the real HOME.
- Its ai-memory hook lines are unchanged (8 on 2.3.2).
- Its bytes were read only to compute its sha256 and mtime and to count the tools/ai-memory-2.3.2 and tools/ai-memory-2.4.0 hook paths (aimem_accept.py cmd_prod_snapshot); nothing from it was printed.

The live server logged the backup request in its own log, which is normal request logging.

switch.method: Cold-copy cutover by the coordinator (cutover.json), following the refuter-corrected switch procedure: stop and quiesce, quiescent fingerprint, at-rest copy, relink bin/ai-memory, upstream install-hooks preview then --apply for both clients, start, live verification, real-client capture.
switch.planned_procedure:
This is not performed here. It is the refuter's corrected steps 5-6 plus the required additions.

Names: ECO=~/.local/share/codex-ecosystem, LIVE=~/.local/share/ai-memory, OLD=$ECO/tools/ai-memory-2.3.2/ai-memory, NEW=$ECO/tools/ai-memory-2.4.0/ai-memory, W=a new private 0700 directory for the window. FP means a mode=ro fingerprint snapshot/compare, as in aimem_accept.py fingerprint/fp_compare or the draft fingerprint.py.

**0. Pre-window gates.**
- v2.4.0 is still the latest release. There is no 2.4.1 or 2.5 and no new advisory against rmcp 2.2.0 or ai-memory 2.4.0.
- The v2.4.0 asset checksum still reads 590f75dd...5076 (the release is not immutable).
- sha256sum $NEW = 360b9dff...6344, and $NEW --version = 'ai-memory 2.4.0'.
- readlink -f $ECO/bin/ai-memory = $OLD, and the 2.3.2 prefix is intact (93eeb299...cfed0).
- Record the known page's body sha256 through a live 2.3.2 memory_read_page just before the window.

**1. Announce to live sessions.** Tell every live Claude Code and Codex session on this host, and the orchestrator:
- the window start and end;
- that ai-memory MCP calls fail while the service is down;
- that Claude hooks keep spooling locally and drain after the restart;
- that the 7 Codex ai-memory hooks will be skipped from the moment ~/.codex/hooks.json changes until the user trusts them in /hooks;
- that sessions should finish or pause tool-heavy work and run /mcp to reconnect afterwards.

No re-login.

**2. Stop and quiesce.**
- Run systemctl --user stop nativestack-memory.service.
- Require pgrep -a -x ai-memory to print nothing (no serve, hook or hook-drain sibling; drains can live up to 5 minutes, so wait or pause sessions).
- Require fuser $LIVE/db/memory.sqlite to print nothing.

**3. Quiescent fingerprint.** FP snapshot $LIVE/db/memory.sqlite -> $W/fp-live-before.json. Expect schema V64 (64 rows) and quick_check=ok.

**4. At-rest (cold) backup.**
- Run mkdir -m 700 $W/cold-v64 && cp -a $LIVE/db $LIVE/wiki $LIVE/config.toml $LIVE/capture-mode $W/cold-v64/.
- FP snapshot $W/cold-v64/db/memory.sqlite -> $W/fp-cold.json.
- FP compare fp-live-before fp-cold 64 must print PASS.
- Treat the copy as secret (config.toml holds auth.token_pepper).
- Optionally also take an online archive before step 2, as a fallback only.

**5. Switch the binary.** Run ln -sfn $NEW $ECO/bin/ai-memory. The unit's ExecStart runs through this symlink. Do not use adoption/bootstrap-linux.sh: it repoints at once and reuses the unversioned download cache.

switch.rollback:
This follows the refuter's cold-copy rollback, which replaces a restore-first approach.

1. Announce to live sessions, then run systemctl --user stop nativestack-memory.service. Require pgrep -a -x ai-memory to print nothing and fuser ~/.local/share/ai-memory/db/memory.sqlite to print nothing.
2. Keep the failed state for salvage: mv $LIVE/db $LIVE/db.v66-failed && mv $LIVE/wiki $LIVE/wiki.v66-failed.
3. Copy back the cold V64 copy: cp -a $W/cold-v64/db $W/cold-v64/wiki $W/cold-v64/config.toml $W/cold-v64/capture-mode $LIVE/.
4. Relink: ln -sfn $ECO/tools/ai-memory-2.3.2/ai-memory $ECO/bin/ai-memory.
5. Restore ~/.claude/settings.json and ~/.codex/hooks.json from the installer's .bak-<ts> files, or re-run the two install-hooks commands with the 2.3.2 binary. Then the user re-trusts the 7 reverted Codex commands in /hooks.
6. Run systemctl --user start nativestack-memory.service.
7. Verify all of the following:
   - ai-memory --version prints 2.3.2.
   - The refinery max version is 64 (64 rows).
   - FP compare fp-live-before against a snapshot of the restored DB at 64 prints PASS.
   - MCP info shows 2.3.2 (exit 0).
   - /healthz returns 404 (2.3.2 has no route).

**Fallback only:** $OLD --data-dir $LIVE restore --from <online archive> --force. It refuses while any process named ai-memory is alive, and it loses every write after the archive. This path was not exercised here. The rollback-artifact proof used a fresh extraction served by 2.3.2 (V64 PASS).

Pages and observations written between the cold copy and the rollback are lost from the live store, but stay in *.v66-failed for manual salvage.

Never start 2.3.2 against the V66 store. The rehearsal showed it exits 1 with 'memory database schema is newer than this ai-memory build' and leaves the store intact, but the service would stay down.

Keep the 2.4.0 prefix for a later retry.
